label: def:covalent-bond-types
title: Covalent bond (shared Hopf links)
html:
Let \mathcal{A}_1 and \mathcal{A}_2 be atoms with residual sub-links R_1 and R_2. In agreement with covalent bond via shared electron braids, each valence electron is the three-strand word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3 whose closure is the positive Hopf link T(2,2) (with the single-component trefoil T_{2,3} retained as the alternative model). A covalent bond of order k is a shared sub-Hopf link

  B_k(R_1, R_2)
  = 
  \underbrace{e^- \oplus \cdots \oplus e^-}_{k \text{ shared electrons } (T(2,2)\text{ closures})}

where each shared electron closure is simultaneously Hopf-linked to one open site in R_1 and one open site in R_2. The integer k is the bond order. The crossing energy of the bond is

  E_{\mathrm{bond}}(k)
  = 
  k \cdot \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(T(2,2)) +
  \binom{k}{2}  \Delta E_{\mathrm{inter}},

where T(2,2) is the Hopf link and \Delta E_{\mathrm{inter}} is the inter-link interaction within the shared sub-link.
